problems.problem_text: State the type of angle (acute, obtuse, reflex, or right angle) for an angle measuring $85^\\circ$.
problems.solution: An acute angle measures between $0^\\circ$ and $90^\\circ$. Since $85^\\circ$ lies between $0^\\circ$ and $90^\\circ$, it is an acute angle.

problems.problem_text: Find the angle $x$ if $x$ and $115^\\circ$ lie on a straight line.
problems.solution: Angles on a straight line sum to $180^\\circ$. Therefore $x + 115^\\circ = 180^\\circ$, so $x = 180^\\circ - 115^\\circ = 65^\\circ$.

problems.problem_text: Four angles meet at a point. Three of them are $72^\\circ$, $108^\\circ$, and $95^\\circ$. Find the fourth angle.
problems.solution: Angles at a point sum to $360^\\circ$. The sum of the three given angles is $72^\\circ + 108^\\circ + 95^\\circ = 275^\\circ$. The fourth angle is $360^\\circ - 275^\\circ = 85^\\circ$.

problems.problem_text: Two straight lines intersect. One of the angles formed is $37^\\circ$. Find the size of the vertically opposite angle.
problems.solution: Vertically opposite angles are equal. Therefore the angle vertically opposite the $37^\\circ$ angle is also $37^\\circ$.

problems.problem_text: Three angles meet at a point on a straight line. One angle is $47^\\circ$, another is $68^\\circ$, and the third is $x$. Find $x$.
problems.solution: The angles meet at a point on a straight line, so they form a straight angle of $180^\\circ$. Therefore $47^\\circ + 68^\\circ + x = 180^\\circ$, so $x = 180^\\circ - 47^\\circ - 68^\\circ = 65^\\circ$.

problems.problem_text: Two lines intersect. Two of the angles are $3x$ and $2x + 20^\\circ$, and they are vertically opposite. Find the value of $x$.
problems.solution: Vertically opposite angles are equal, so $3x = 2x + 20^\\circ$. Subtracting $2x$ from both sides gives $x = 20$.

problems.problem_text: Two angles on a straight line are $(2x + 10)^\\circ$ and $(3x - 20)^\\circ$. Find the value of $x$ and the size of each angle.
problems.solution: Angles on a straight line sum to $180^\\circ$. So $(2x + 10) + (3x - 20) = 180$. Simplifying: $5x - 10 = 180$, so $5x = 190$, giving $x = 38$. First angle: $2(38) + 10 = 86^\\circ$. Second angle: $3(38) - 20 = 94^\\circ$.

problems.problem_text: Four angles meet at a point. They are $x^\\circ$, $(x + 20)^\\circ$, $(x + 40)^\\circ$, and $(x + 60)^\\circ$. Find the value of $x$ and the size of each angle.
problems.solution: Angles at a point sum to $360^\\circ$. So $x + (x + 20) + (x + 40) + (x + 60) = 360$. Simplifying: $4x + 120 = 360$, so $4x = 240$, giving $x = 60$. The angles are $60^\\circ$, $80^\\circ$, $100^\\circ$, and $120^\\circ$.

problems.problem_text: Two straight lines intersect. Four angles are formed: $a^\\circ$, $b^\\circ$, $c^\\circ$, and $d^\\circ$. Given that $a = 3x - 15$, $b = 2x + 25$, and $a$ and $c$ are vertically opposite to each other, find the values of $a$, $b$, $c$, and $d$.
problems.solution: Since $a$ and $b$ are on a straight line, $a + b = 180$. So $(3x - 15) + (2x + 25) = 180$, giving $5x + 10 = 180$, $5x = 170$, $x = 34$. Then $a = 3(34) - 15 = 102 - 15 = 87^\\circ$? Wait, let me recalculate: $3 \\times 34 = 102$, $102 - 15 = 87$. $b = 2(34) + 25 = 68 + 25 = 93^\\circ$. Check: $87 + 93 = 180 \\checkmark$. Since vertically opposite angles are equal, $c = a = 87^\\circ$ and $d = b = 93^\\circ$.

problems.problem_text: Five angles meet at a point. They are $x^\\circ$, $2x^\\circ$, $3x^\\circ$, $(x + 30)^\\circ$, and $(2x - 18)^\\circ$. Find the value of $x$ and the largest angle.
problems.solution: Angles at a point sum to $360^\\circ$. So $x + 2x + 3x + (x + 30) + (2x - 18) = 360$. Simplifying: $9x + 12 = 360$, so $9x = 348$, $x = 38.666...$ That doesn't give nice numbers. Let me recheck: $x + 2x + 3x + x + 30 + 2x - 18 = 9x + 12$. $9x + 12 = 360$, $9x = 348$, $x = \\frac{348}{9} = \\frac{116}{3} \\approx 38.67$. The angles would be $38.67^\\circ$, $77.33^\\circ$, $116^\\circ$, $68.67^\\circ$, $59.33^\\circ$. Largest is $3x = 116^\\circ$.

problems.problem_text: On a straight line $AOB$, $\\angle AOC = (5x - 10)^\\circ$, $\\angle COD = (3x + 20)^\\circ$, and $\\angle DOB = (4x - 10)^\\circ$. Find $x$ and the measure of $\\angle COD$.
problems.solution: Angles on a straight line sum to $180^\\circ$. So $(5x - 10) + (3x + 20) + (4x - 10) = 180$. Simplifying: $12x + 0 = 180$, so $12x = 180$, $x = 15$. Then $\\angle COD = 3(15) + 20 = 45 + 20 = 65^\\circ$.

problems.problem_text: Two lines intersect at $O$, forming vertically opposite pairs. One angle is $(5x - 7)^\\circ$ and its adjacent angle is $(3x + 11)^\\circ$. Find the four angles.
problems.solution: Adjacent angles on a straight line sum to $180^\\circ$. So $(5x - 7) + (3x + 11) = 180$. Simplifying: $8x + 4 = 180$, $8x = 176$, $x = 22$. First angle: $5(22) - 7 = 110 - 7 = 103^\\circ$. Adjacent angle: $3(22) + 11 = 66 + 11 = 77^\\circ$. By vertical opposite angles, the four angles are $103^\\circ, 77^\\circ, 103^\\circ, 77^\\circ$.

problems.problem_text: Prove that if two adjacent angles are equal and lie on a straight line, then each is a right angle.
problems.solution: Let the two equal adjacent angles be $x^\\circ$ each. Since they lie on a straight line, their sum is $180^\\circ$. Therefore $x + x = 180$, so $2x = 180$, giving $x = 90$. Hence each angle is a right angle ($90^\\circ$).

problems.problem_text: In the diagram, $AB$ and $CD$ are straight lines intersecting at $O$, with $\\angle AOC = 58^\\circ$. $OE$ bisects $\\angle AOC$, and $OF$ bisects $\\angle BOD$. Find $\\angle EOF$.
problems.solution: Since $\\angle AOC$ and $\\angle BOD$ are vertically opposite, $\\angle BOD = 58^\\circ$. $OE$ bisects $\\angle AOC$, so $\\angle AOE = \\angle EOC = 29^\\circ$. $OF$ bisects $\\angle BOD$, so $\\angle BOF = \\angle FOD = 29^\\circ$. Now $\\angle AOC + \\angle COB = 180^\\circ$ (straight line), so $\\angle COB = 180^\\circ - 58^\\circ = 122^\\circ$. Similarly, $\\angle AOD = 122^\\circ$. $\\angle EOF = \\angle EOC + \\angle COB + \\angle BOF = 29^\\circ + 122^\\circ + 29^\\circ = 180^\\circ$.

problems.problem_text: Prove that the bisectors of two vertically opposite angles are opposite rays (i.e., lie on the same straight line).
problems.solution: Let two lines intersect at $O$, forming vertically opposite angles $a$ and $c$ (equal) and $b$ and $d$ (equal), with $a + b = 180^\\circ$. Let $OX$ bisect $a$, so $\\angle XOa = \\frac{a}{2}$. Let $OY$ bisect $c$, so $\\angle YOc = \\frac{c}{2} = \\frac{a}{2}$. Since $a$ and $c$ are vertically opposite, $\\angle XOY = \\frac{a}{2} + b + \\frac{c}{2} = \\frac{a}{2} + b + \\frac{a}{2} = a + b = 180^\\circ$. Therefore $X$, $O$, and $Y$ are collinear; i.e., $OX$ and $OY$ are opposite rays.

problems.problem_text: At a point $O$, seven rays emanate dividing the full angle into seven angles. The smallest angle is $x^\\circ$, and each subsequent angle is $5^\\circ$ more than the previous. Find $x$.
problems.solution: The angles form an arithmetic sequence: $x, x+5, x+10, x+15, x+20, x+25, x+30$. Sum of angles at a point = $360^\\circ$. Sum = $7x + (0+5+10+15+20+25+30) = 7x + 105 = 360$. So $7x = 255$, $x = \\frac{255}{7} \\approx 36.43^\\circ$.
